title.narrative: Recovery of Economic Activity for Informal Sector Employment (REALISE)
Återhämtning av ekonomisk aktivitet för det informella sysselsättningsprojektet

description.narrative:
Projektutvecklingsmålet (PDO) är att öka tillgången till inkomstmöjligheter för utsatta inom den informella sektorn som respons på kriser, utöka inkomst- och försörjningsstödet till hushåll som lever i fattigdom och med osäker tillgång till mat och förbättra effektiviteten i att hantera sociala skyddsprogram i Liberia. Detta kommer att uppnås genom att stödja hushållen att återuppliva småföretag; arbetsintensiva offentliga arbeten och stöd för anställningsbarhet; samhällsutveckling och jordbruksstöd; systemuppbyggnad för målinriktning och social kontantöverföring; samt kapacitetsuppbyggnad, projektgenomförande och samordning.
Ambassadens totala bedömning är den föreslagna insatsen är högst relevant från ett fattigdomsperspektiv och har potential att skapa en positiv förändring av levnadsvillkoren hos de som lever i extrem fattigdom, sårbarhet och marginalisering. Den föreslagna samfinansiering och ytterligare finansieringen har visat sig vara en unik och effektiv kanal för ambassaden att i större utsträckning nå de mest sårbara hushållen som lever i fattigdom i Liberia. Insatsen står ut som högst relevant för ambassadens investeringar i Liberia, då det är en förutsättning för att säkerställa mänskliga rättigheter och ett effektivt verktyg att påverka multidimensionell fattigdom.

The Project Development Objective (PDO) is to increase access to income-earning opportunities for the vulnerable in the informal sector in response to crises, expand income and livelihood support to poor and food insecure households, and improve efficiency in managing social protection programs in Liberia. This will be achieved by supporting households to revive small businesses; labor-intensive public works and employability support; community development and agriculture support; systems building for targeting and social cash transfer; capacity building, project implementation and coordination.
The embassy's overall assessment is that the proposed intervention is highly relevant from a poverty perspective and holds potential to significantly improve living conditions of people living in extreme poverty, vulnerability, and marginalization. The proposed basket-fund and Addition Financing (AF) has emerged as a unique and highly effective channel for the embassy to at scale reach the poorest and most vulnerable households in Liberia. This contribution stands out as a highly relevant for the embassy investment in Liberia, as it is a human right and an especially effective tool to impact on multidimensional poverty.

title.narrative: Administration Agreement between Sida and IBRD and IDA (Trust Fund No. 073901)

description.narrative:
To illustrate results achieved, below are results from the report on fourth quarter of 2024. Results reporting is focused on outputs and cover the full project, to which Swedish funding is one of the funding sources (also French Development Agency and World Bank IDA funding).
Component 1 (support to small businesses):1395 beneficiaries received Small Businesses support for the final round of implementation in 18 communities in Montserrado and Margibi Counties. 724 of these are categorized as new businesses, while 671 are categorized as already existing businesses.
Component 2 (Temporary Employment Support and Employability development for Vulnerable workers): 5000 beneficiaries were recruited in 50 communities in Montserrado and Margibi Counties for labor intensive public work (not only Q4 2024). Tool Grants were paid to 196 Beneficiary working groups from 50 communities in Montserrado and Margibi County.
Component 3 (Capacity building and project implementation and coordination): Regular monitoring of project activities was carried out for all components. Occupational Health and Safety training for the REALISE Project Team as well as Environmental Health and Safety Training for Project Beneficiaries were conducted. A series of communication activities were conducted to promote project visibility, including: The REALISE Hour Radio Show, Project quarterly Newsletter and Newspaper advertisement.
Component 5 (Community Livelihood and Agriculture Support): A total of 5360 beneficiaries (accumulated during the project period) across 8 implementing counties have fully received second tranche payment. In all project communities across the 8 counties, beneficiary farming groups have started to harvest varieties of crops. Beneficiaries and Community Oversight Committees were equipped with knowledge and skills to make informed decisions for improved productivity and income generation. Farmer Based Organizations or Trade Groups are providing market linkage support and small scale value addition activities for beneficiaries in all project communities. As they link beneficiaries to these buyers, constraints faced by farmers to sell their produce and avoid wastage is reducing.
Component 6 (Social cash transfer): 11 253 households were registered for social cash transfers in Grand Bassa, Grand Kru and Rivercess counties during the fourth quarter of 2024. 9 591 were enrolled in the Social Cash Transfer Program and 4 914 households received first quarter cash transfers.
